link_notes: The linked paper and repo (pgmpy) describe a general-purpose probabilistic graphical model toolkit; data simulation is only one feature, so it is not a dedicated synthetic-data method.

open_release.rationale: Simulation from user-defined or example networks is offered, but the sources never frame the output as a release or privacy-preserving substitute.

pipeline_testing.rationale: Nothing in the README or docs frames simulated data as test data for software or formats.

ml_augmentation.rationale: No use of simulated data to train predictive models or augment training sets is described.

statistical_replication.rationale: The toolkit fits parameters from data and simulates, but no fidelity evaluation of the simulated data is shown in the digest.

causal_inference.rationale: The README presents simulation under specified evidence or interventions from causal graphical models.

quotes.text: Generate synthetic data under specified evidence or interventions.
pgmpy provides the building blocks for causal and probabilistic reasoning using graphical models.

education.rationale: Tutorial and example notebooks exist for the library, but they teach pgmpy generally rather than synthetic data generation.

quotes.text: Built-in collection of example Bayesian Networks and datasets from different sources.

benchmarking.rationale: The library ships standard example networks but the sources do not position it as a baseline or benchmark for generators.

imbalance_correction.rationale: No class-imbalance or minority-class framing appears in the sources.
